content.text: Film approval is ready for confirmation: both concept-level checks show creative approval does not grant release. Scheduling remains unresolved on whether night shoots are allowed. Give me the update. The architect holds film-production and scheduling.

Film examples are approved by me, and I have settled scheduling: night shoots are allowed under the same reservation rules as daytime shoots.

For film production, my decision in this turn is to approve the creative-approval examples. For scheduling, my decision in this turn is to permit night-time reservations under the existing rules.

Creative acceptance does not grant release permission. Scheduling approval reserves a date and time, not creative acceptance; night hours do not change that reservation's meaning, so the same reservation rules apply at night.

These are my decisions for the two topics.

The supplied film checks establish the creative-approval distinction.

The film outcome is creative acceptance without release authority.

Next, lead, realize the approved film examples. Also commission an independent review of those same film examples.
